title: Split a unit only when success changes
statement: Split a knowledge unit only when what counts as a right answer changes, and keep variants of difficulty, representation and method inside it.
detail: The reading course's curriculum-architecture notes fork a knowledge unit only when its success condition changes and absorb difficulty, representation and method variants into the unit instead of spawning new ones (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/train-teacher/references/curriculum-architecture.md`, lines 50-51 and 81). A curriculum BrainLift gives the same forking rule and calls a systematic performance shift across representations the clearest sign that a unit is mis-sized or mis-specified: learners who master it in text-based items but fail it as a diagram, graph or symbols are showing evidence about the unit's boundary, not an item quirk (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback1/Curriculum & Knowledge BrainLift.md`, lines 268 and 549).
against: The same BrainLift reads such a drop as either several units collapsed into one or a unit that needs representation-specific supports, so the signal can call for a split even when the right answer is the same (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback1/Curriculum & Knowledge BrainLift.md`, line 549).

evidence.quote: **fork a KC only when the success condition changes**.
Forking a KC should be reserved for cases where the success condition changes.
The clearest sign that a KC is mis-sized or mis-specified is systematic performance shift across representations.
that is not an item quirk — it is evidence about the KC boundary.
Either you are looking at multiple KCs collapsed into one, or the KC requires explicit representation-specific affordances that the current specification doesn't acknowledge.
